_meta.note: Hand-written synthetic transcripts designed to be hard. Every prospect company and every person named here is fictional. Real vendor product names (Gong, Clari, HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho) appear only as tools or competitors mentioned in conversation; nothing here describes those vendors' real products, pricing or customers. The seller throughout is an unnamed call-recording-to-CRM vendor. No real call audio or customer data.
_meta.scoring_note: Each case carries a 'rationale' field next to 'expected'. It is part of the answer key: strip both before sending transcripts to a model. Segments carry start/end timestamps in seconds; the original easy set has none.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Hey Dana, thanks for hopping on. So, um, where did we land with IT?

segments.speaker: PROSPECT
segments.text: Yeah, so, IT has your questionnaire. The one you filled in. They're going through it now, it's like ninety questions, so it's taking a minute.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Right, yeah, I sent that back last Tuesday with the SOC 2 summary attached, so hopefully that covers most of it.

segments.speaker: PROSPECT
segments.text: It does, mostly. Okay so here's what I'll do. I'll get you the signed-off questionnaire, or whatever comments they have, by Friday. And Hamid, our IT lead, he said he'll check whether the phones can even do dual-channel recording.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Okay, perfect. Honestly that's the main thing. There's nothing I need to do until that comes back.

segments.speaker: PROSPECT
segments.text: Good, because I'm, like, buried this week. Oh, and I'm going to book half an hour with Maureen, our practice director, probably week after next, so she can see the numbers before anything gets signed.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Makes sense. Is there anything you want from me for that, or is the deck I sent enough?

segments.speaker: PROSPECT
segments.text: No, the deck's fine, I've got it. I'll just walk her through it.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Great. Then yeah, ball's in your court, Dana. Just reply on the same thread when IT's done.

segments.speaker: PROSPECT
segments.text: Will do. Thanks, Sam.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Cheers, speak soon.

next_steps: Dana sends IT's sign-off or comments on the security questionnaire by Friday
Hamid (IT lead) checks whether the phones support dual-channel recording
Dana books half an hour with Maureen (practice director), probably week after next, and walks her through the deck

cases.rationale: Traps 1, 2 and 8: every forward promise ('I'll get you the signed-off questionnaire by Friday', the Maureen meeting, the walkthrough) is the prospect's or their colleague's, and the rep's only first-person actions (questionnaire, SOC 2 summary, deck) were already done. The rep explicitly says there is nothing to do until IT replies, so the rep commitment list is empty.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Imran, hi, thanks. So I know you had a list of, um, open questions from last time?

segments.speaker: PROSPECT
segments.text: Yeah, a few. First one, the contract. Did legal ever get the MSA? Because I haven't seen it.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: So I sent the MSA over yesterday afternoon, to you and to, uh, Bethany in legal. Might be in spam, it had a big attachment.

segments.speaker: PROSPECT
segments.text: Ah, okay, I'll check. Second thing, the pilot. Thirty days feels short for us, honestly, because of the lettings cycle.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Yeah, I get that. So if legal's okay with it on our side, I could probably stretch the pilot to sixty days. I just can't say yes to that myself.

segments.speaker: PROSPECT
segments.text: Okay. And pricing? We need numbers for the budget meeting.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Honestly I can't promise pricing this week. Finance is mid quarter-close and everything's stuck behind that. Next week's more realistic, but I don't want to give you a date and then miss it.

segments.speaker: PROSPECT
segments.text: Fair. Last one, the Welsh-language thing. Like half our tenant calls in Cardiff are in Welsh.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Yeah, so, I'll try and see whether Welsh transcription is anywhere on the roadmap. I genuinely don't know, so no promises there.

segments.speaker: PROSPECT
segments.text: Okay. So what actually happens next?

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: What I will do is send you the pilot success criteria doc tomorrow morning, so you can mark it up before we talk about the length.

segments.speaker: PROSPECT
segments.text: Great. I'll share that with our ops manager when it lands.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Perfect. Thanks, Imran.

rep_commitments: Send the pilot success criteria document tomorrow morning
next_steps: Imran checks spam for the MSA
Imran shares the pilot success criteria document with the ops manager

cases.rationale: Trap 2, all four forms: the MSA was already sent (done), the sixty-day pilot depends on legal (conditional), pricing is explicitly declined with no date, and the Welsh roadmap check is 'I'll try and see... no promises' (hedged). Only the success criteria document is an unconditional rep commitment.

cases.rationale: Trap 3 (with trap 4, competitor in passing): two commitments exist only as short replies to the prospect's requests ('Yeah, sure, Thursday's fine'; 'that's on my list for today'), so the deliverable and deadline must be taken from the prospect's turn; the third is the rep's own offer, accepted, then confirmed with a date and invite. Gong is named as a tool they evaluated for the same job, so it counts, consistent with the original set counting a previously trialled tool.

segments.speaker: REP

cases.rationale: Trap 4, lookalikes: 'clarify' appears four times with no mention of Clari, 'outreach' is the generic word for their cold calling, and 'gong' is a physical gong on the sales floor. No vendor is named at all, so competitors is empty.

segments.speaker: REP

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: So, Wendy, you've had the quote for a week now. How's it landing?

segments.speaker: PROSPECT
segments.text: Honestly, it's fine, but the seat count's wrong. We're at forty reps now, not twenty-five. We hired a whole night shift.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Oh, congrats. Okay, so I'll redo the quote for forty seats, same per-seat price, and you'll have it tomorrow.

segments.speaker: PROSPECT
segments.text: Great. And look, at forty seats, can you do fifteen percent off? If you can, I think we sign by the thirtieth.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: I hear you. I can't do fifteen, that's just not something I'm able to offer. What I'll do is ask my manager whether there's any room on a two-year term, and I'll come back to you by Tuesday either way.

segments.speaker: PROSPECT
segments.text: Okay. And we'd need it live by January fifth, that's when the new contract with the retailer kicks in.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: January fifth is tight. I don't want to commit to that until onboarding has looked at your setup. I'm not saying no, I'm just not saying yes yet.

segments.speaker: PROSPECT
segments.text: Fine. I'll send you the shift rota so onboarding can see what they're dealing with.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: That'd help, thanks.

rep_commitments: Send a revised quote for 40 seats at the same per-seat price tomorrow
Ask the manager whether there is any pricing flexibility on a two-year term and reply by Tuesday

cases.rationale: Trap 5: '15% off', 'sign by the thirtieth' and 'live by January fifth' are said only by the prospect; the rep refuses the discount and explicitly withholds the go-live date. A correct answer contains neither figure. The rep's real commitments are the 40-seat requote and the manager question with a Tuesday reply.

cases.rationale: Trap 6: Priya is the seller's SE, so her demo is a selling-side commitment even though the rep does not own it; Tomasz's recordings and Ruth's whitelisting are the prospect's colleagues and belong in next steps, not rep commitments. Marco 'might be able to hop on, if he's free' is hedged and excluded.

rep_commitments: Send Kev the API usage and rate-limit document by end of day tomorrow, copying Rob
next_steps: Rob shares Kev's email address in the chat
Rob takes it to Shona (finance director) for sign-off after Kev's review, aiming for before the end of Q1

cases.rationale: Trap 7: 44 turns with the only real rep commitment at turn 21, surrounded by decoys: 'I'd want to check with our product team' is hedged, the summary for Shona is an offer the prospect defers, and 'I'll let you go' in the small-talk ending is a sign-off. Salesforce is the prospect's CRM, not a competitor; Gong was trialled for the same job and counts.
